newsitem.title: UK: UK sees no reason for major Zaire force-sources.
newsitem.headline: UK sees no reason for major Zaire force-sources.

text.p: Britain does not see any reason to send a large-scale multinational force to Zaire because a British reconnaissance mission found a comparatively small number of refugees, defence sources said on Monday.
They said the aerial mission over eastern Zaire had identified only around 200,000 refugees and displaced people compared with the 700,000 the United Nations initially believed were there.

One of two British battalions standing by to join such a force to bring aid to refugees displaced by fighting between Hutu rebels and the Zairean army was likely to be stood down this weekend, he said.

Ambassadors from 14 countries gave the go-ahead over a week ago to send a Canadian-led multinational force to Zaire, but the organisers have not yet chosen whether to opt for airdrops or deploying ground troops to escort aid convoys.

More than 20 countries including Britain, the United States, France, Belgium, Senegal and South Africa are to contribute to the mission, more likely to comprise 1,000 or 2,000 troops than the 10,000 originally planned.
